Project Highlighting
Role Solo UX, research + design
Year Mar–May 2026
Company Clarivate, Derwent Innovation

Highlighting, redesigned.

A core feature of a global patent search tool, taken from a single keyword utility to a concept-level system. Solo, research to dev-ready spec.

16
Usability sessions, run solo.
14/14
Rated the new Mini Map a must-have.
8
Features designed and handed to dev.
Context

Users stayed, but worked around us.

Derwent's highlighting gave users one word per colour, no grouping, no overview, no templates. Competitors had moved past that years ago, and some users were patching the gap with third-party plugins rather than leaving the platform. With no PM and no researcher on the team, I ran the whole project solo, 16 sessions, recruited, facilitated, and synthesised.

The work

Three views, one panel.

The highlighting panel re-architected around how patent researchers actually read. Each view answers a different question, and users switch between them depending on the task.

01 Minimap Must-have · 14/14

Where do my concepts cluster? Compressed view of the whole patent — coloured marks per section, scannable at a glance.

02 List Must-have · 14/14

Query terms load themselves. Additional terms come from a saved template. One click to hide a concept, arrows to jump between hits.

03 Matrix Design decision

Concept × section grid with hit counts. Tested badly inside one record — users wanted presence, not raw numbers. Kept it here, but the real home for this view is the search-results page.

"It lets you jump directly to where all terms appear together."

P3 · IP Strategy Manager

The rest, in brief

Four more features.

The remaining features that came out of the same 16 sessions. Three of these I prototyped fixes for mid-study — one dropped a discoverability failure from 8/8 to 0/5 between rounds.

04 Must-have
Multiple words per colour

One colour, one concept, many synonyms grouped. The foundation everything else builds on.

05 Must-have
Icon discoverability fix

8/14 couldn't find the config icons. Swapped for labelled buttons mid-study. 0/5 failures after.

06 High
Proximity highlighting

When two concepts appear near each other, both get emphasised. Arrows show the relationship without users needing query syntax.

07 Should-have
Smart string parsing

Paste a full search string. Operators and parentheses become concept boundaries automatically.

How I worked

Four choices that shaped it.

Concepts, not keywords

One colour, one concept, multiple synonyms. The way users actually think about patents.

Reuse over invention

Every new element reuses an existing pattern. Nothing new to learn.

Move it, don't kill it

The Matrix flopped inside a record but worked at results level. Same component, different home.

Fix in the room

Three changes applied mid-study. When friction hit three users in a row, I changed the prototype before the next session.

Where it stands

Research done, design done, dev next.

Stories written, dev presentation scheduled. The win-back metric: whether users who left Derwent highlighting for third-party tools come back, and stay.
